title: Work as worship
hookLine: kirat, honest labor, is itself devotion

lines: A CARPENTER'S BREAD. A RICH MAN'S FEAST.
cards: Two dinner invitations arrive on the same evening. One comes from a carpenter named Lalo, a poor man who works with his hands. His table has coarse bread.
The other comes from Malik Bhago, a rich official throwing a grand feast, who expects the holy man in town to attend. The janamsakhis say Guru Nanak stayed with Lalo and didn't go to the feast.
Bhago was offended, and demanded to know why. You heard this story in year one. Today it carries an idea.

teach.b: The tradition says Guru Nanak took a piece of Lalo's coarse bread in one hand and a piece of Bhago's rich food in the other, and squeezed. From Lalo's bread came milk. From Bhago's came blood.
The point lands without a speech: one meal was earned by honest hands; the other was squeezed out of other people.

That's kirat: honest work, earning a living by your own effort without cheating anyone. We met it beside the farmer who can't make it rain, named alongside remembering the Name and sharing. Today it gets its own story.
In a salok, Guru Nanak puts it in a line.

teach.h: EAT WHAT YOU EARN, GIVE FROM YOUR HAND.
teach.b: In paraphrase: the one who eats what they have earned by their own work, and gives some of it from their hand, Nanak, that one recognizes the path. Notice the order. First the earning.
The path is recognized in the work, not only in the temple. Why can work be worship?

teach.h: THE WORKBENCH AS A PLACE OF PRAYER.
teach.b: If freedom can come while laughing and eating, as Guru Arjan said three days ago, it can come at a workbench too.
Fixing a sink, teaching a class, stocking shelves, driving a delivery route, caring for a patient at night: done honestly, each is a kind of devotion.
Not because the job is holy in itself, but because honesty in it is a way of remembering the One. Lalo's bread was ordinary. What made it sweet was how it was earned.

how: Sikhs speak of kirat karni, earning an honest living by one's own work, as part of the path alongside remembering the Name and sharing, and tell the story of Bhai Lalo and Malik Bhago to show it.

o: work done only inside a temple or gurdwara
a rule to rest from all work on holy days
honest work, done well, as a form of devotion

p: a rich official with a feast
honest work by your own effort

s: in the story, Guru Nanak chose the rich man's feast
the janamsakhis say he stayed with Lalo, the carpenter.
Guru Nanak links earning by your own work with recognizing the path
eat what you earn, and give from your hand.
kirat means any work at all, honest or not
it means honest work, earned without cheating anyone.

games.q: you're a traveling teacher, and both a poor carpenter and a rich official invite you to dinner the same night. what do you do?
o: go to the rich man's feast; he can help many people.
stay with the carpenter and eat his coarse bread.
games.why: the janamsakhis say Guru Nanak stayed with Lalo, and when Bhago demanded why, squeezed milk from Lalo's bread and blood from Bhago's food.

practice: Bring to mind the next piece of work in front of you, paid or unpaid, a report, a shift, homework, laundry, a repair, and picture doing it all the way through without one shortcut you'd be embarrassed to explain.
No padding the hours, no blaming someone else, no cutting the corner nobody would see. Notice how that feels in the body, and if you pray, offer the work with Waheguru.

wordCard.voice: Work as worship. Kirat, honest work, earned by your own effort, which Sikh teaching treats as devotion itself. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: work is worship. Honest bread, honestly earned, gives milk in the story. See you tomorrow.
